"Udviklingsmålet på ≥95%" (The development target of ≥95%) is a politically established policy benchmark for Indicator 3 in the Danish national quality report for atrial fibrillation, published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Programme (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut). Indicator 3 specifically measures adherence to clinical guidelines recommending TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) testing at the time of a new atrial fibrillation diagnosis to rule out underlying thyroid disease. 

Despite its importance in driving quality development within Danish cardiology, the ≥95% target is currently unmet at the national level, with reports indicating no significant improvements over the past three years [^src1]. The shortfall is pervasive across the entire healthcare system; no individual regions and no health clusters (sundhedsklynger) have succeeded in achieving the target for this indicator [^src1]. 

The universal failure to reach the ≥95% benchmark signals a systemic challenge in implementing the clinical guideline. This widespread underperformance is analyzed alongside systemic data and organizational barriers, such as issues related to LABKA coding and SundK data transfers, which complicate the accurate measurement and execution of the recommended clinical practices.
